title: Add migration dry-run, atomic rollback hooks, and pre-upgrade backup verification
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Private deployments require predictable, auditable upgrades. Operators need a way to validate schema migrations and backups before cutting over, and a robust automated path to roll back when an upgrade introduces incompatibilities. This PR introduces three coordinated safety primitives: 1) a migration dry-run mode that executes migrations against an ephemeral clone of state and produces a deterministic migration report; 2) Helm lifecycle hooks and installer-managed markers that enable atomic rollback paths if post-upgrade health checks fail; and 3) pre-upgrade backup capture and checksum verification integrated into the installer and the Terraform preflight. Goals: reduce upgrade-induced incidents, provide an operator-friendly verification step, and make automated rollback safe and auditable. What I changed (high level): - installer/commands: add `redwoodctl upgrade --dry-run` which 1) snapshots volumes (PVC or local) into a temporary clone, 2) spins up a migration sandbox using the same chart values but isolated k8s namespace, 3) runs the DB and index schema migrations against the clone, and 4) returns a migration report (SQL changes, estimated row touch, affected indices). - helm charts: add pre-upgrade hook templates (pre-upgrade-job, post-upgrade-validation) plus a rollback marker secret that the installer monitors. Charts include a new values flag `migrations.rollbackGuard.enabled`. - terraform modules: add an explicit state-lock-and-validate step for private deployments (Terraform run will now create a managed lock resource and run `terraform plan` with a validation pass against a cloned infra state when `upgrade_dry_run=true`). - backup/restore: the installer now captures a compressed backup and computes a SHA256 checksum; the dry-run compares checksum after clone/restore to confirm fidelity. - health checks and rollback: if the post-upgrade validation job fails, the installer will automatically trigger the Helm rollback and initiate a verified restore from the pre-upgrade backup. A failure path includes detailed logs and a fail-open option for emergency manual intervention. Checklist (implemented): [x] redwoodctl dry-run command and CLI UX [x] sandbox namespace orchestration + cleanup [x] Helm pre/post hooks and rollback marker secret [x] Backup capture (PVC snapshot or file-level tar) + SHA256 verification [x] Terraform validation + state lock resource [x] Integration test harness for dry-run path [x] Documentation for operators and runbooks How to exercise locally: 1) Build the installer binary: make build-installer 2) Create a development cluster and deploy a representative private deployment (see docs/quickstart-dev.md) 3) Run `redwoodctl upgrade --target-version vX.Y.Z --dry-run` 4) Inspect the generated report at /tmp/redwood-upgrade-report-<ts>.json and verify checksums 5) Try a simulated failing validation by toggling `migrations.postUpgradeValidation.failOn=true` in the chart values to force a rollback Notes on safety and design choices: - The dry-run uses an isolated namespace and ephemeral PVCs so production workloads are not affected. - We rely on storage provider snapshot semantics when available, otherwise we fall back to file-level tar+rsync. - Migration dry-run is intended to be deterministic; it records SQL statements and row counts observed in the sandbox, but operators should still run smoke tests against application behavior. - Automatic rollback is conservative: we only rollback if the validation job exits non-zero and the rollback marker secret has not been manually cleared. - Terraform changes are additive and introduce a managed lock resource; no mutable provider behavior is required. Risks and mitigations: - Long-running dry-runs may increase I/O load on shared storage: dry-run can be scoped to specific services via flags. - Storage providers without snapshot support will have slower clone times: documented fallback and operator warnings added. - False positives in validation: validation job logs are retained for 7 days and include re-run commands to reproduce the failure. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag default-off 2) Dogfood on internal staging private cluster for 2 weeks 3) Gradual opt-in for customer upgrades via support-assisted channels 4) Promote to default for all private deployments after 30 days and no regression incidents Metrics to monitor post-release: - % of upgrades that used dry-run mode - Frequency of automatic rollbacks and root cause categorization - Time for dry-run + sandbox cleanup - Backup verification failure rate Related work: ENG-2178 (schema-versioning), infra/terraform#402 (state-lock work), docs/ops-runbooks#39 (runbook additions).

release_notes: Added `redwoodctl upgrade --dry-run` to validate migrations and backups before production cutover.
Installer will capture a pre-upgrade backup and verify checksum before performing upgrade; automatic rollback on validation failure is now supported (opt-in behind chart flag).
Terraform modules include an optional managed state lock and plan validation step for safer upgrades.
